# Tidepool

> Tidepool is a zero-dependency IDE for software developers, written in Rust from the ground up by Joseph Abbott III, with no third-party crates: its own OS bindings, rasterizer, font renderer, UI toolkit, text engine, parsers, protocols and terminal emulator. https://jabbott.dev/Tidepool/ shows its gate and two example programs of its libraries, run on each commit of `main` that passes CI, its architecture, and its features with how far each has come.

Key facts:

- Status: in development, at version 0.1: on Linux, cargo tp opens a window that shows the first frame, jabbott.dev's backdrop and a line in each bundled face, and does nothing else yet. {{build_line}}
- Language: Rust {{toolchain}}, edition 2024; {{crates}} crates in the workspace; third-party crates: {{third_party}}
- Planned: a native GUI in jabbott.dev's design language and a terminal UI with vim-style modal editing; first-class Rust (rust-analyzer, cargo) and Markdown; managed toolchains (rust-analyzer, git, the JDK, the Android SDK and NDK, bundletool, Xcode) installed and driven through their official channels; Android and iOS builds, signed and verified; AI through language agents speaking the Tidepool Agent Protocol, and offline predictive text
- Targets: Linux x86_64 (X11 and XWayland), macOS 13 and later (universal), Windows 10 1809 and later (x86_64)
- License: Apache-2.0
- Source: {{repository_url}}
- Author: Joseph Abbott III, software engineer (https://jabbott.dev/resume/)

## The gate

`cargo xtask ci`, which CI runs on Linux, macOS and Windows for every pull request and every push to `main`; this page is published only from a commit of `main` that passed it on all three. Here: {{gate_line}}. Its summary:

## Architecture

The page draws two views, which {{repository_url}}/blob/{{commit}}/diagrams/c4-architecture.md also draws, with every module and edge:

- Containers: the developer sees Tidepool through its GUI frontend, which shows the first frame today (roadmap M2.6), or is to use its terminal UI (M7.1), both parts of the tidepool binary, which opens the GUI's window and draws that frame (M2.6). The binary reads its settings, through the workspace's settings from M4.7 (M3.4, M4.6, M4.7), and is to write other TOML files (M5.1), open, edit and save the developer's workspace folders (M4.3), install and run managed tools such as curl, rustup and cargo, rust-analyzer, git, the Android SDK and Xcode as child processes (from M5.1), and speak the Tidepool Agent Protocol over stdio to language agents (M9.3); the reference agents reach model servers through curl or loopback HTTP (M9.6). The core binary opens no sockets but its connection to the local X server, over a Unix socket only (ADR-0039).
- Crates by layer: 26 crates in seven layers, each using only crates below it that its row of the dependency matrix names. Built: core (M0.2, M1.6, M1.8) and sys, its crate root (M0.1) and Linux declarations (M2.1, M2.2, M2.7), in layer 0; codec (M1.4 to M1.7, and QOI, M2.4), text (M1.1 to M1.3), gfx, the CPU rasterizer and backdrop (M2.3), font, the TrueType parser and glyph rasterizer (M2.8) and the glyph atlas, text layout and fallback (M2.5), and platform, its crate root (M0.1), the Linux window, events, waker and present over X11 (M2.2), and the clipboard and folders (M2.7), in layer 1; ui, its widget tree, layout, focus, input routing, draw lists and accessibility tree (M3.1), its theme (M3.2), its controls (M3.6), its collections, tab strip, splitter, card and code block (M3.7), and its overlays, the modal dialog, tooltip, toast, and command palette (M3.3), and workspace, its folders and ignore files, trust and settings (M4.7), in layer 2; gui, which draws the first frame (M2.6) and paints ui's draw lists (M3.5), in layer 4; the binary, which opens its window, in layer 5 (M0.1, M2.6); xtask (from M0.3) and bench (M1.9, M2.5, M3.3) in layer 6. Only sys and platform may hold unsafe code.
